Several open-source frameworks exist to reduce the amount of glue code
needed to build a RAG system. LangChain provides composable building
blocks for chaining together document loaders, text splitters, retrievers,
and language model calls, and is widely used for general-purpose LLM
application development. LlamaIndex is more specialized: it focuses
specifically on connecting large language models to external data through
indexing and retrieval abstractions, and is often preferred when the data
layer is the hardest part of a project.

On the retrieval side, FAISS is the most common local vector search
library, while Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, and Milvus are common choices
when a managed or self-hosted vector database is needed at production
scale. On the generation side, RAG can sit in front of essentially any
large language model, including proprietary APIs such as Anthropic's
Claude models and OpenAI's GPT models, or open-weight models such as
Llama or Mistral that a team hosts itself.

Choosing a stack usually comes down to three questions: how much data
needs to be indexed, how much control over infrastructure the team wants,
and whether the generation step calls an external API or runs a
self-hosted model. Small class projects and prototypes typically favor
FAISS plus a hosted LLM API, since it needs no dedicated infrastructure
and can be built and demonstrated on a single laptop.
